title: Expropriation notices for sanitary and stormwater utility land
subtitle: Land acquisition authority after closed session, a declared conflict of interest, and a short special meeting.
overview: Council held a short special meeting and authorized the City Solicitor to serve and publish Notices of Intent to Expropriate for five properties on Sydney Street South, Ottawa Street South, Borden Avenue South and Courtland Avenue South (partial). The land is part of the municipal land acquisition strategy for a sanitary and stormwater utility {{vote:m1}}.

Staff said the full expropriation process typically takes 18 to 24 months. Affected property owners have already been notified and contacted directly. The notice step opens the formal process, and owners can still negotiate with the City.

After a closed session, Council authorized the Chief Administrative Officer to approve and sign an acquisition of an interest in land, as long as the deal stays within the approved budget in the staff report {{vote:m3}}. The minutes do not say which property is involved. One councillor declared a conflict on a closed-session land acquisition item because of nearby property ownership and took no part in it.
The meeting lasted about two hours including the closed session.

decisions.detail: The City Solicitor can serve and publish notices of intent to expropriate under the Expropriation Act for five properties on Sydney, Ottawa, Borden and Courtland streets for the sanitary and stormwater utility.

decisions.item: Land acquisition authority from closed session
decisions.detail: The CAO may approve and sign an acquisition of an interest in land, to the City Solicitor's satisfaction, provided it falls within the budget in report DSD-2024-271.
Council agreed to meet in closed session after the special meeting on two solicitor-client privilege matters and a land acquisition matter.

debate: One councillor asked staff to outline the timing of the expropriation process. Staff said the notice would be posted publicly for three weeks in the local paper. Next come negotiation with landowners, registering the plan, notice of intent to take possession, and an offer of final compensation. Staff estimated 18 to 24 months in total.

A councillor asked what engagement had taken place with property owners. Staff said much of it was confidential because it concerned potential acquisitions, and gave no property-specific detail. Staff did say owners had been notified and expected this step.
There was no recorded debate on the closed-session land acquisition motion, and no delegations appeared.
